- Columns: Category, Identifier, Description
- Total requirement rows: 52
- Top requirement categories: (uncategorized) (38); Administrative operation (1); Availability and portability (1); Client Access and Session (1); Consultation and cancellation of reservations (1); Customer Profile (1); Environment administration and preparation (1); Flight booking (1); Flight inquiry (1); Integrity and traceability (1)
- Representative requirement rows:
  - [RF - 01] | category=Client Access and Session | The system must allow the customer to access their account via login and password.
  - [RF - 02] | The system must create a usage session after successful authentication.
  - [RF - 03] | The system must allow the customer to close their session through logout.
  - [RF - 04] | The system must require an active session to access restricted areas, such as customer profile and reservations.
  - [RF - 05] | category=Flight inquiry | The system must allow searching for flights by informing the origin airport, destination airport and travel date.
  - [RF - 06] | The system must allow one-way or round-trip travel searches.
  - [RF - 07] | The system must display the flight options found for each leg of the trip.
  - [RF - 08] | The system must display, for each flight found, information on departure time, arrival time and reference values ​​for the classes displayed to the customer.
  - [RF - 09] | The system must work with a set of previously registered airports.
  - [RF - 10] | category=Flight booking | The system must allow an authenticated customer to book an outbound flight.
  - [RF - 11] | The system must allow an authenticated customer to book round-trip flights in the same operation.
  - [RF - 12] | The system must generate an identifier for each reservation created.
  - [RF - 13] | The system must record the date on which the reservation was made.
  - [RF - 14] | The system must inform the customer of the identifier of the reservation created after completing the operation.
  - [RF - 15] | category=Consultation and cancellation of reservations | The system must allow the customer to consult their existing reservations.
  - [RF - 16] | The system must present the customer with a list of reservations already made.
  - [RF - 17] | The system must allow canceling a selected reservation.
  - [RF - 18] | After cancellation, the reservation should no longer appear as active in the customer's listing.
  - [RF - 19] | category=Customer Profile | The system must allow the customer to consult their own profile.
  - [RF - 20] | The system must display the customer's contact details in the profile, including telephone number, telephone type and address.
  - [RF - 21] | The system must allow updating the customer's contact details and address.
  - [RF - 22] | The system must require the customer's current password to confirm changes to the profile.
  - [RF - 23] | The system must prevent a client from consulting or changing another client's profile.
  - [RF - 24] | category=Loyalty program | The system must display to the customer their status in the loyalty program.
  - [RF - 25] | The system must display the number of miles accumulated during the year.
  - [RF - 26] | The system must display the total number of miles accumulated.
  - [RF - 27] | Loyalty information should be presented to the customer as query data, not as edit fields in the main interface flow.
  - [RF - 28] | category=Environment administration and preparation | The system must allow initial loading or reloading of the application database.
  - [RF - 29] | The loading process must allow defining the number of example clients to be generated.
  - [RF - 30] | The base payload must recreate key operation data, including flights, customers, sessions, and test bookings.
  - [RF - 31] | The system must provide summary operating information, such as number of customers, sessions, flights, segments, reservations and registered airports.
  - [RNF - 32] | category=Security and access control | The application must restrict private functionalities to authenticated clients.
  - [RNF - 33] | The client session must have limited validity and automatically expire after the configured period.
  - [RNF - 34] | Logout should invalidate the session in use immediately.
  - [RNF - 35] | Customer personal data must be protected against undue access by other customers.
  - [RNF - 36] | category=Performance and scalability | The application must support a high volume of calls and queries, especially in the authentication, flight search and reservation flows.
  - [RNF - 37] | Flight queries should prioritize quick responses, as they represent a recurring flow in the customer journey.
  - [RNF - 38] | The solution must be suitable for growth in usage without relying on manual fulfillment for core self-service operations.
  - [RNF - 39] | category=Availability and portability | The application must be able to run in different environments, including local infrastructure, public cloud and hybrid scenarios.
  - [RNF - 40] | The solution must keep customer, flight, session and reservation data persisted between application requests.
  - [RNF - 41] | category=Integrity and traceability | Each session and each reservation must have a unique identification.
  - [RNF - 42] | Reservation and cancellation operations must maintain sufficient consistency to correctly reflect the current state of the customer's reservations.
  - [RNF - 43] | The application must record minimum data for monitoring operations, such as reservation date and count of operational records.
  - [RNF - 44] | category=Usability and self-service | Navigation should favor self-service, allowing the customer to search for flights, manage reservations and update their profile without human intermediation.
  - [RNF - 45] | The system must present times, dates and values ​​in a way that is legible to the customer.
  - [RNF - 46] | The main journeys must be accessible via a simple web interface, with clear separation between flight search, reservations, profile and support.
  - [RNF - 47] | category=Administrative operation | The environment must offer a simple means of preparing and checking the database for testing, demonstrations or operational restart.
  - [RNF - 48] | The system must provide basic operating indicators to monitor the environment without requiring direct consultation of the database.
  - [RNF - 49] | category=Scope remarks identified | The flow called `Check-in` in the interface, in practice, works as querying and canceling reservations; A complete passenger check-in process was not identified in this repository.
  - [RNF - 50] | There is a `Support` interface with the appearance of a real-time chat, but the corresponding backend was not found in the analyzed code. Therefore, this item was not treated above as a consolidated functional requirement.
  - [RNF - 51] | No public registration flow for new customers was identified. Customer accounts are generated by administrative data loading routine.
  - [RNF - 52] | No payment flow, seat choice or formal fare class selection was identified at the time of booking; the system displays prices, but the reservation observed in the code is simplified.
